chapter: Second European tour and the crash
title: First concert by a Black band in Copenhagen
summary: The Chocolate Kiddies Orchestra gives its own concert in February 1931 at the Odd Fellow Palais and then about ten others.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So, what year was it you went into this business. Was it after the crash in '29?
No, it was, that was, yeah, right after the same year, or the beginning of 1930.
So I went on and I was taking engagements, and I ended up in Valencia in '31.
Yeah. And so, from then, after we finished Valencia, that's we -- where we try giving our first concert. Black concert.
Yeah. You were the first black band to give a concert. And was that the Christmas concert in Copenhagen?
No. This was a concert of our own. We gave it in the concert hall. I mean, the symphony hall. What's that man's name, now? At that time -- I guess he's dead, now.
Maybe that was the name. Anyhow, ---
Wilhelm Hanson. He was the big music publisher and promoter on Broadway.
Yeah. Well, we gave it there and it was such a success that we moved on to other places there. And we moved on to Sweden.
That was February 5, 1931. You gave this concert.
And it was still called, "Sam Wooding and his Chocolate Kiddies Orchestra". And that was in the, where was it, in the Oddfellow Palais?
Yes, which is a big concert hall.

Now you see, from then on we went to Sweden and did the same thing. And made one or two of the lesser cities. And we give, I guess, about ten or eleven of those concerts in all. The last one was in Vienna, I think.
